thread:
alex: Heads up — canary deploy for gpu-provisioner in eu-west-1 errored out. Looks like the CI used a decrypted creds.yaml with an old VAULT_TOKEN, so the provisioner fell back to the default pool and we hit capacity errors. :grimacing:

maya: saw the alert graph. which job ran? can you paste the CI log snippet?

alex: job name `ci/deploy/eu/gpu-provisioner/canary`

alex: log excerpt:
```
[2026-03-18T09:12:02Z] sops: decrypted secrets/infra/gpu/creds.yaml
[2026-03-18T09:12:03Z] export VAULT_TOKEN=redacted-old-token
[2026-03-18T09:12:04Z] helm upgrade --install gpu-provisioner ./charts/gpu -f creds.yaml --set image.tag=canary
[2026-03-18T09:12:18Z] kube api: provisioner assigned pool: gpu-default
[2026-03-18T09:12:21Z] ERROR: pool gpu-default capacity exceeded
```

ben: that token string matches one we rotated last week for prod. CI runner probably pulled a cached decrypted artifact instead of re-decrypting with the new SOPS age key.

jordan: @alex can you confirm the artifact SHA the deploy step actually read? my hunch is the chart and the secrets came from different SHAs.

alex: CI printed artifact path `s3://ci-artifacts/k8s/decrypted/run-7f3a2b9/creds.yaml` but chart commit in the deploy manifest points at `sha-9c2d1a4`. artifacts bucket has a `latest` symlink that might be racing.

maya: so this is decrypted-artifact drift — deploy step picks `latest` instead of the per-run path. pipeline flow should pin all artifacts to the run ID.

ben: quick mitigation: stop the canary, patch the deployment to clear VAULT_TOKEN so the provisioner uses the node-assigned role rather than the stale token. that reduced the immediate risk.

alex: did `kubectl -n infra set env deploy/gpu-provisioner VAULT_TOKEN=""` to force vault role auth. still saw a short spike in pool allocation while old pods drained.

ci-bot: @channel CI job `ci/deploy/eu/gpu-provisioner/canary` failed 3 times in 18m — https://ci.internal/redwood/jobs/1234

jordan: long-term fixes I propose:
- stop publishing decrypted secrets to a global `latest` path; write per-run pinned paths (run-id or sha)
- switch deploy-time secret access to Vault OIDC short-lived tokens issued for the runner instead of shipped decrypted files
- add a pre-deploy integrity check that compares checksums of chart commit vs secrets artifact

maya: +1. also add a CI guard: after `sops --decrypt` compute checksum and record it to the pipeline metadata; fail if the `aws s3` object we plan to use has a different checksum.

ben: found another root cause: CI runner age key TTL was 30d but we rotate SOPS keys every 14d for prod. the runner keyring cached the old key so `sops --decrypt` produced stale tokens unless we force keyring refresh.

alex: commands to reproduce locally on a runner:
```
sops --decrypt creds.yaml | sha256sum
aws s3 cp s3://ci-artifacts/k8s/decrypted/latest/creds.yaml - | sha256sum
```
Both commands returned different hashes for the same deploy attempt. confirms cached decrypt vs object.

jordan: concrete action items:
- alex: update CI to always write decrypted secrets to `s3://ci-artifacts/k8s/decrypted/<run-id>/creds.yaml` and pin the deploy step to that path — ETA: today
- maya: add Vault OIDC workflow for deploys and document the flow — ETA: EOD tomorrow
- ben: change runner bootstrap to invalidate sops age key cache and add a cache-bust step in the job — ETA: tomorrow morning
- ops-bot: author a runbook for "decrypted artifact drift" and a monitor rule to detect checksum mismatches — created KB ticket below

ben: temporary safety net: add a small post-deploy helm test that queries provisioner pool assignment and fails the job if the pod lands in the wrong pool. prevents silent capacity overcommit during canaries.

alex: rolling canary back to stable and pushing the CI pinning change in a PR now. posting monitoring screenshots in 30m. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: runbook created: `KB-3821 - Decrypted artifact drift during CI deploys` https://wiki.internal/redwood/kb/KB-3821

maya: we'll also check eu-west GPU allocations and the billing spike. tagging finance/infra-costs for follow-up.

alex: noted — will report back in 30m with allocation graphs and any cost delta. :eyes:
